items.title: Rule-out yield in older and kidney patients
items.whyItMatters: Most studies report pooled results, and the one study of older and kidney patients found low rule-out rates (claim c4); the unit's time saving depends on it.
items.opportunity: Extract rule-out yield and safety by age and kidney function wherever reported and estimate the local yield from the unit's case mix.

items.title: Sampling time failures at peak hours
items.whyItMatters: Late second samples were common (claim c3) and change how patients are classified.
items.opportunity: Include studies reporting timing failures and the fixes that reduced them.

items.title: Specialist centre evidence applied to a district hospital
items.whyItMatters: Safety estimates come mostly from specialist centres with younger patients.
items.opportunity: Tabulate setting and age for every included study and grade indirectness explicitly.

items.title: Older patients waiting longest
items.whyItMatters: If the pathway mainly speeds up younger patients, older patients may wait as long as now while the unit reports improvement.
items.opportunity: Report time saved separately for patients aged 75 or over.

errorsFound: The proposal assumes the published rule-out rate of about 57 percent will apply locally; the unit's older case mix makes that unlikely.
reevaluation: The rapid review should report safety, rule-out yield and time saved by age and kidney function, and treat sampling-time failures as a core question rather than a footnote.
summary: Four gaps; rule-out yield in older and kidney patients and sampling failures are high severity.
